## 1. GLOBAL MACRO OVERVIEW

The June CPI print released Tuesday was the pivotal inflection point this report series had been building toward. CPI came in at +3.5% YoY — a dramatic deceleration from May's 4.2% three-year high — driven almost entirely by energy prices falling 5.7% MoM (the largest monthly drop since April 2020) as the brief US-Iran ceasefire in June brought relief at the pump. Core CPI eased to 2.6% YoY and was flat month-on-month, with motor vehicle insurance falling 2.0% the second consecutive month [Source: https://www.reuters.com/business/us-consumer-inflation-slows-more-than-expected-june-2026-07-14/]. IBD's live coverage confirmed S&P 500 futures turned higher immediately after the data, with the headline 12-month rate undercutting the 3.8% forecast by 30 basis points — labelled "shockingly cool" [Source: https://www.investors.com/news/cpi-inflation-june-federal-reserve-warsh-testimony-oil-prices-sp-500/]. The FRED macro bundle now reflects this updated inflation picture: CPI YoY at 3.73% (as of June), down from the prior 4.27% May reading, with fed funds effective at 3.63% [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL; https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FEDFUNDS]. The 10-year Treasury yield has risen to 4.62% and the 2-year to 4.26% as of July 13 [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10; https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS2] — yields are elevated but the curve is no longer pricing the acute July hike that had reached 46.5% probability on Monday.

However, the relief was short-lived in crude oil markets. Trump's reimposition of a full naval blockade of Iranian ports — described as a "third consecutive night of strikes" by US military — has driven Brent back above $85 for the third consecutive session and sent gold lower from Tuesday's post-CPI high near $4,100 back to $4,034.70 (-0.65%) [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/15/gold-slips-as-oil-rally-keeps-inflation-rate-outlook-on-investors-radar.html; Yahoo Finance (GC=F)]. CNBC's Wednesday morning report notes the dynamic precisely: "Trump continues to maintain the blockade of ships that is flowing out of the Strait of Hormuz, causing oil prices to rise and gold to come under pressure" [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/15/gold-slips-as-oil-rally-keeps-inflation-rate-outlook-on-investors-radar.html]. The IEA estimates Gulf crude and condensate exports increased 6.5 million bpd in June to 16.1 million bpd — representing 85% of the total recovery — but the renewed blockade threatens to undo this partial restoration [Source: https://oilprice.com/Energy/Crude-Oil/The-Next-Oil-Rally-May-Depend-On-China-Not-The-Middle-East.html].

The Bank of America Global Fund Manager Survey, released Tuesday, shows global investor sentiment at its highest since February, with cash allocations falling to an "uber-low" 3.6% — a level that triggered BofA's contrarian sell signal — and a record share of respondents expecting a "no landing" for the global economy [Source: https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/global-investors-turn-bullish-since-february-bofa-survey/]. This extreme bullish positioning, combined with a still-unresolved Hormuz crisis and resurgent oil prices on Wednesday morning, creates a fragile setup: any hawkish surprise from Warsh's congressional testimony today could accelerate a positioning unwind.

OPEC on Monday lowered its 2026 oil demand growth forecast for the third consecutive month to 780,000 bpd, while raising its 2027 outlook — a confirmation that the Gulf production disruption from the Iran war is embedding into forward demand projections [Source: https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/opec-further-lowers-2026-global-oil-demand-growth-forecast-2026-07-13/]. The next oil rally's trajectory may depend more on China than the Middle East, per OilPrice.com analysis — China demand recovery is the variable that could either amplify or dampen the Hormuz premium [Source: https://oilprice.com/Energy/Crude-Oil/The-Next-Oil-Rally-May-Depend-On-China-Not-The-Middle-East.html].
